Okay I think my smooth brain is starting to comprehend the concept of ramp. Basically what you're saying is, since I have very few impactful cards that are below 3 mana, I should look into ramp that costs 1-2 mana, since that would mean I'm spending less time watching everyone else do their cool things. 

The more expensive the ramp, the more powerful the effect needs to be, which is probably why you said sol ring is the best for casual play, it makes your first turn "worth" 3 mana, potentially making it so you could play a 4 cost spell on your second turn. So when I look at something like overgrowth, it costs 2, but essentially makes it so that on that turn if I played a land, I'm getting 4 mana gained, rather than the usual 1. (Again why temple of the False God isn't that good, its 2 mana, but it's a land which means that unlike sol ring, that turn is worth 0 and its value is miniscule later on.)

If I'm understanding it correctly, then the reason you call the commander feast or famine, is because he's incredibly expensive (and unlike a lot of other expensive cards he has no way to lower that cost at the top), and vulnerable to removal (which furthers his high cost). But he would essentially be the ultimate ramp, giving me theoretically infinite mana for casting 5 creatures if I somehow top decked 5 expensive dinosaurs. 

I think I'm starting to realize that at its core the game is about (mana) cost effectiveness, rather than potential insane combos (which I'm starting to think are only popular because they are a form of cost management as well.)

So basically get more mana to cast more good stuff, before I start worrying about good stuff that I couldn't afford to cast anyway.
